pthm-tgr-finite-entropy-balance.iff-forward: R Statement and Proof 2.1 apply the slab identity to S, and 3.1 deduces monotonicity when side flux vanishes. Neither nonnegative entropy change nor zero integrated production is claimed to characterize the adopted local second law.
pthm-tgr-finite-entropy-balance.iff-reverse: R Proof 3.1 concludes equal endpoint charges from vanishing production with zero side flux; it never infers pointwise production or impermeability from equality of charges. Thus there is no entropy-balance converse to discharge.

texp-tgr-insulated-entropy-region.iff-forward: R Statement imposes vanishing pullback on every side face; Proof 1.1 integrates it and 2.1 substitutes zero flux into the balance. This prediction is an implication from an ideal boundary, not a classification.
texp-tgr-insulated-entropy-region.iff-reverse: R Proof 3.1 only substitutes the extra zero-production assumption; equal endpoint charges are not used to reconstruct the pointwise impermeable boundary. No reverse worldtube claim is present.

pthm-tgr-local-first-law.iff-forward: R Statement gives differential and Euler identities for the adopted parcel energy. Proof 1.1 differentiates the density and 1.2 differentiates the supplied parcel function; it does not characterize which materials admit that state function.
pthm-tgr-local-first-law.iff-reverse: R The cancellation in Proof 2.1 yields Gibbs–Duhem and 3.1 yields parcel Euler equality. Neither identity is used to recover the material postulate or its domain, so no converse constitutive assertion exists.

pthm-tgr-perfect-entropy-circulation.iff-forward: R Proof 1.1 specializes the isolated balances and 2.1 derives the loop derivative, then uses spatially constant specific entropy as a sufficient condition. The displayed advection and circulation equations are conclusions, not equivalences.
pthm-tgr-perfect-entropy-circulation.iff-reverse: R Statement expressly warns that material advection does not imply spatial constancy; Proof 2.1 likewise does not infer constant specific entropy from a vanishing loop integral. There is no reverse circulation characterization.

pthm-tgr-dissipative-local-admissibility.iff-forward: R Proof 2.1 substitutes four adopted dissipative closures, and 3.1 proves the resulting quadratic production nonnegative on the rest space. It claims these closures suffice, not that entropy admissibility determines them.
pthm-tgr-dissipative-local-admissibility.iff-reverse: R Statement disclaims causality, stability and solution existence, while Proof 3.1 uses nonnegative coefficients only in the forward direction. Nonnegative divergence is not asserted to reconstruct viscosities, conductivity or diffusion.

pthm-tgr-bulk-extended-entropy.empty: C Statement requires a nonempty open solution region and, for the witness, supplies a state point and O=(-cδ,∞)×R³ with δ>0. Proof 1.2 gives constant fields on that explicit nonempty product; no empty solution family is used.
pthm-tgr-bulk-extended-entropy.iff-forward: R Proof 1.1 derives the corrected entropy divergence from an actual bulk solution, and 1.2/2.2 verify a separate homogeneous witness. Those are conditional deductions, not a characterization of every solution.
pthm-tgr-bulk-extended-entropy.iff-reverse: R Proof 3.1 proves positivity for nonzero amplitude and vanishing at zero amplitude in the explicit exponential witness. It does not infer the corrected relaxation law from the entropy identity for arbitrary fields.

pthm-tgr-radiation-local-properties.iff-forward: R Proof 1.1 changes velocity normalization and 2.1 applies the radiation balance supplier; 3.1 computes frozen acoustic eigenvalues. No converse reconstruction of the radiation equation of state is claimed.
pthm-tgr-radiation-local-properties.iff-reverse: R The Statement limits its acoustic conclusion to a uniform-rest frozen submodel. Proof 3.1 never infers a nonlinear radiation material from sound speed c/√3; the two transverse zero modes are not a reverse criterion.

def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers.one: R Definition fixes a Lorentzian four-manifold and the rank-three rest-space shear; a singleton event is not the nonempty open spacetime domain. There is no adjustable one-dimensional or one-cell index.
def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers.degenerate: C Definition requires future timelike ξ and T>0, and defines Nξ=√(-g(ξ,ξ))>0 before dividing by Nξ and kBT. Null/zero generators and zero temperature are therefore excluded explicitly.
def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers.endpoints: R Definition takes smooth fields on open O and positive-temperature values in (0,∞). It asserts no extension to the boundary of O, zero-temperature limit or complete Killing orbit endpoint.
def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers.iff-forward: C Definition first requires ξ to be Killing and explicitly invokes thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities for the equivalent symmetric-derivative criterion. This is the forward direction of the cited defining equivalence, not a missing new proof.
def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers.iff-reverse: C The same Definition identifies the symmetric covariant Killing equation as equivalent by its named GR supplier. Applying that exact supplied equivalence recovers the Killing criterion; no thermal-normalization constancy is inferred.

def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure.one: R Definition specifies one fiber at a fixed event with three real momentum coordinates; it is not an indexed cell construction. Borel singleton shell sets are allowed and receive the ordinary positive-density Lebesgue measure, with no separate particle-count branch.
def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure.degenerate: C Definition assumes M*>0, so E(q)≥M*>0 even at q=0. Thus the density 1/E is continuous and finite at rest; no massless singular density is admitted.
def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure.endpoints: R The shell is parametrized over all R³ without a finite radial cutoff. Definition claims a Borel measure via a nonnegative density, not finiteness of its total mass or an integral limit at infinity.
def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure.iff-forward: R The mass-shell Definition introduces the pushforward measure and verifies its positivity; the equality P⁰=E(q) only unpacks the already selected future sheet. No equivalence between a measure property and dynamics is asserted.
def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure.iff-reverse: R Tetrad independence is deferred to the named discharge lemma; this Definition does not assert that an arbitrary Borel measure with some property must have density d³q/E. There is no reverse uniqueness classification.

lem-tgr-isometry-natural-tensor-invarian.one: R Statement permits all finite covariant derivative orders; the first derivative is included by Proof 3.1 because the preserved connection commutes with pullback. Fixed spacetime dimension is four, not a one-dimensional branch.
lem-tgr-isometry-natural-tensor-invarian.degenerate: C Statement assumes a smooth nondegenerate Lorentzian metric and nowhere-zero ξ. Proof 1.1 uses its local flow and 2.1 uses uniqueness of the metric-compatible connection; neither a degenerate metric nor a zero-generator flow-box is invoked.
lem-tgr-isometry-natural-tensor-invarian.endpoints: R Statement restricts preservation to common open local-flow domains. Proof 1.1 starts at the identity flow parameter and differentiates locally; no continuation to a maximal-flow endpoint or complete group is claimed.
lem-tgr-isometry-natural-tensor-invarian.iff-forward: R The implication runs from a Killing field through local isometry in Proof 1.1 to connection preservation in 2.1 and curvature operations in 3.1. It is not an equivalence between scalar invariants and Killing symmetry.
lem-tgr-isometry-natural-tensor-invarian.iff-reverse: R Proof 3.1 proves that preserved connection and vector determine preserved natural tensors; it never concludes a metric isometry from equality of selected curvature scalars. Such a converse is outside the statement.

lem-tgr-mass-shell-polynomial-rigidity.one: R Proof 1.1 varies a unit spatial direction and radius; one shell vector alone would not imply rigidity and is not the quantified hypothesis. Statement requires the identity on every future massive-shell vector.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-polynomial-rigidity.endpoints: C Proof 1.1 divides only by 2r with r>0; 2.1 compares coefficients on z>M, so the rest point r=0 need not be divided by. The separate null clause uses ρ>0 and excludes the zero vector.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-polynomial-rigidity.nonempty-choice: C Facts F1 supplies a Lorentz orthonormal basis and a finite sign adjustment to its timelike vector; Proof 2.1 tests finitely many coordinate and pair directions. No family of frames across spacetime is selected.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-polynomial-rigidity.iff-forward: R Statement assumes the quadratic-plus-linear expression vanishes on the whole shell and concludes vanishing coefficients. Proof 1.1/2.1 establishes this massive rigidity implication, with a separate null-cone conclusion.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-polynomial-rigidity.iff-reverse: R The null conclusion in Proof 3.1 allows a metric multiple instead of the massive zero tensor. The lemma presents these as two implication clauses; a converse polynomial classification is not a separately stated obligation.

lem-tgr-mass-shell-measure-tetrad-invari.one: R The theorem compares two tetrads at one fixed event, and Proof 3.1 treats every Borel set including singletons. There is no singleton family of frames or variable spatial dimension to specialize.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-measure-tetrad-invari.degenerate: C Statement assumes M*>0; Proof 1.1 obtains det C=M*²/E, and 2.1 cancels M*² using that positivity. Mass zero is excluded and is not covered by this determinant argument.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-measure-tetrad-invari.endpoints: R The map Q in Proof 1.1 is a global diffeomorphism of R³, and 3.1 applies nonnegative Borel change of variables without a radial-boundary limit. No finite interval endpoint is part of this measure comparison.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-measure-tetrad-invari.iff-forward: R Proof 2.1 obtains the Jacobian ratio between already supplied future tetrads and 3.1 proves equality of their measures. The conclusion is tetrad independence, not an iff test for a matrix to be Lorentz.
lem-tgr-mass-shell-measure-tetrad-invari.iff-reverse: R Facts F2 assumes Lorentz basis changes before the Jacobian calculation. Equality of two measures is not used to reconstruct orthonormality, future orientation or a unique tetrad, so no reverse claim is made.

thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments.one: R Statement includes the Bessel order j=1 explicitly; Proof 1.1 bounds each of orders zero through three and derives the K1 shell formula. No one-particle probabilistic ensemble is asserted by the density n.
thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments.degenerate: C Statement requires positive M*,kB,T,n,c and reference action. Proof 1.1/2.1 proves finite strictly positive integrals, so normalization and logarithm in 3.1 are legitimate; zero mass or zero temperature is outside these formulas.
thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments.iff-forward: R The result constructs a probability density and evaluates its current/stress moments; Proof 3.1 normalizes an already defined partition function. It does not characterize all distributions having ideal-fluid moments.
thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments.iff-reverse: R Rest-frame symmetry in Proof 4.1 and pressure integration in 5.1 establish moments of the specified exponential. No conclusion reconstructs the exponential from a perfect stress tensor or the ideal-gas pressure identity.

ex-tgr-flrw-no-killing-equilibrium.one: R The example has three spatial directions and a varying positive length-time coordinate. Proof 2.1 rules out a timelike Killing field on every nonempty open region, not merely at one sampled event.
ex-tgr-flrw-no-killing-equilibrium.nonempty-choice: C Proof 3.1 selects one point of a hypothetical nonempty U and a coordinate ball around it, an ordinary finite existential choice. Facts A1 separately carries ACω through the smooth geometry; no global frame family is chosen.
ex-tgr-flrw-no-killing-equilibrium.zero: C The specified domain is s>0 with L0>0, so Proof 1.1 may use 1/s and 1/L0 and 2.1 may use s^-3. The singular zero-scale endpoint is excluded, while vanishing spatial components in 2.1 give a nonnegative norm contradiction.
ex-tgr-flrw-no-killing-equilibrium.iff-forward: C Although clauses (a)/(b) are nonexistence deductions, Proof 4.1 explicitly derives the null-shell equivalence: vanishing Liouville derivative for every null vector gives dζ=0 and symmetric derivative λg by F4.
ex-tgr-flrw-no-killing-equilibrium.iff-reverse: C Proof 4.1 also checks the reverse null-shell criterion: constant ζ and conformal Killing β give zero derivative because g(P,P)=0, then directly constructs β=b(s/L0)∂s. This corrects the earlier blanket no-iff disposition.

lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization.one: R Multiplying ξ by b=1 in Proof 3.1 leaves lapse, congruence and inverse-temperature field unchanged. The argument uses one connected open domain rather than a variable particle or cell count.
lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization.degenerate: C From F1, Nξ and T are strictly positive. Proof 1.2 therefore has f=(kBNξT)^-1>0 and valid contractions with timelike u; Proof 2.1 obtains a positive constant TK rather than a zero-temperature branch.
lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization.endpoints: R The constant-normalization theorem is local on open O; Proof 2.1 uses convex coordinate balls and connectedness. It does not extend the lapse normalization to horizons where ξ ceases to be timelike.
lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization.nonempty-choice: C Proof 2.1 joins two supplied points inside one convex coordinate ball by its explicit straight segment. Those local calculations prove constancy and connectedness glues level sets; no simultaneous choice of global curves is required.

lem-tgr-thermal-killing-kinematic-equiva.one: R The rest-space trace in Proof 2.2 is three, as fixed by the Lorentzian four-manifold. No dimension-one shear formula is claimed, and one isolated scalar condition cannot replace the four stated conditions.
lem-tgr-thermal-killing-kinematic-equiva.degenerate: C Statement takes g(u,u)=-1 and T>0; Proof 1.1 can divide by kBT and 2.1 can pass from D log T to DT. A null observer or zero-temperature vector is excluded by these hypotheses.
lem-tgr-thermal-killing-kinematic-equiva.endpoints: R The kinematic equivalence concerns smooth pointwise fields on open O. No limit at T=0 or at a boundary of the observer domain is asserted; each contraction is evaluated at admitted points.
lem-tgr-thermal-killing-kinematic-equiva.nonempty-choice: C Proof 1.1 and 2.1–2.3 use algebraic projections along the supplied u; 3.1 invokes the pointwise direct-sum decomposition. No observer or tetrad has to be chosen over an indexed set.

thm-tgr-massive-juttner-stationarity.one: R The entire shell, not one momentum sample, is quantified in Statement and Proof 3.2; one sample would not support the polynomial-rigidity supplier. The pointwise normalizer classification concerns a fixed event with three momentum coordinates.

ex-tgr-uniform-perfect-background.iff-forward: R Verification 1.1 checks the explicit constant-state fields solve the adopted balances, then 2.1 contracts their stress with a boost. It proves an example and an observer formula, not a classification of all perfect fluids.
ex-tgr-uniform-perfect-background.iff-reverse: R The zero-boost reduction in Verification 2.1 recovers the chosen rest density only. It does not infer the material model or prescribed Minkowski background from an observed energy density.

ex-tgr-homogeneous-bulk-entropy.iff-forward: R Verification 2.1 checks the chosen homogeneous stress/current balances and 2.2 checks the corrected relaxation law. The result is an explicit exponential witness, not an equivalence defining all admissible bulk fields.
ex-tgr-homogeneous-bulk-entropy.iff-reverse: R Verification 3.1 distinguishes zero and nonzero amplitude for this supplied witness. It does not infer an exponential time dependence or the model law from positive production alone.

lem-tgr-countable-l2-completeness.empty: C F1 takes a supremum over all finite subsets, including the empty subset whose sum is zero. Proof 1.1 and 2.1 finite-sum bounds remain valid for it; the zero sequence belongs to the space, so the ambient Hilbert space is not empty.
lem-tgr-countable-l2-completeness.degenerate: C The zero vector has zero norm by F1; a Cauchy sequence identically zero has all coordinate limits zero in Proof 1.1 and the convergence bound in 2.1 still holds. No positive norm is used as a denominator.
lem-tgr-countable-l2-completeness.iff-forward: R Statement asserts completeness of the sequence norm and then invokes the Hilbert-space definition F3. Proof 1.1 constructs coordinate limits and 2.1 proves norm convergence, without an equivalence classifying other sequence spaces.
lem-tgr-countable-l2-completeness.iff-reverse: R The completeness proof ends with every Cauchy sequence converging in the given norm. There is no claim that every Hilbert space is this countable sequence space or a reverse identification of its index set.

thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization.empty: C Statement assumes r≥1 and every d_i≥1. Thus the product basis in Proof 2.1 has at least one vector; 3.1 gives each Zi a nonempty finite sum of positive exponentials. Empty cells and zero-dimensional tensor factors are excluded.
thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization.iff-forward: R Proof 1.1 substitutes the charged redshift identities, then 3.1 computes factorization for independent cells. It does not claim every Gibbs state or interacting reduced state has this tensor factorization.
thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization.iff-reverse: R Neutrality is used in Proof 5.1 to identify the two already defined dynamics. Factorization of a density is not used to recover the charged geometry, stationarity or absence of interactions.

thm-tgr-kms-orbit-time-rescaling.empty: C Statement supplies a normalized state on a unital algebra; its state convention gives ω(1)=1, excluding the zero algebra. For any A or B equal to zero, the zero strip function satisfies both rescaled boundary identities in Proof 1.1.
thm-tgr-kms-orbit-time-rescaling.degenerate: C Statement requires λ>0, βK>0 and ℏ>0; Proof 1.1 divides by λ and 1.2 multiplies by λ without collapsing the strip. At λ=1 both constructions are the original strip function.

thm-tgr-finite-response-redshift.empty: C Statement fixes one nonzero finite-dimensional cell inherited from the factorization theorem. Proof 1.1 uses its normalized density; even if A or B is zero, 2.2 gives the zero commutator/control contribution with the same finite-time bound.
thm-tgr-finite-response-redshift.iff-forward: C Proof 3.1 contains an actual subsidiary equivalence: commutation with Gloc implies commutation with σ because the Gibbs density is its spectral function; the following variance reduction uses precisely this condition.
thm-tgr-finite-response-redshift.iff-reverse: C Proof 3.1 uses injectivity of the real exponential on the finite spectrum to show σ and Gloc have the same eigenspace decomposition. Commutation with σ therefore implies commutation with Gloc. The old blanket no-reverse row missed this explicit proof claim.

prop-tgr-rotating-mode-gibbs-obstruction.empty: C The occupation index N0 contains zero and its empty finite subsum equals zero in F1. Proof 1.1 shows finite-support vectors lie in the diagonal domain and are dense; e0 is present, and the partition series in 1.2 begins with weight one.

ex-tgr-proper-clock-qubit-response.empty: C The Example uses C², not a variable-dimensional or empty cell. Verification 1.1 sums exactly two positive Gibbs weights and 2.2 gives the two spectral lines; neither normalization is an empty sum.
ex-tgr-proper-clock-qubit-response.zero: C The Example explicitly allows Q=0 and evaluates the static derivative at λ=0. Verification 3.1 has R(0)=Δ/2>0, so no division by zero occurs; ℏ>0 is the physical-time convention of F1 thm-tgr-finite-response-redshift, and Δ,N>0 are given.
ex-tgr-proper-clock-qubit-response.degenerate: C The positive gap Δ and lapse N keep the two frequencies distinct and the periods finite. Verification 3.1 gives R(λ)≥Δ/2 for all real λ, so its hyperbolic quotient stays defined even at zero control.
ex-tgr-proper-clock-qubit-response.iff-forward: R Verification 2.1 directly multiplies Pauli matrices and 3.1 evaluates a re-prepared static family. These establish the displayed qubit formulas without asserting that every oscillatory response comes from this model.
ex-tgr-proper-clock-qubit-response.iff-reverse: R Verification 4.1 excludes a dc relabelling because the supplied sinusoid persists. It never infers a two-level Hamiltonian from a measured spectral pair, and contains no reverse model-classification assertion.

lem-tgr-spatial-shear-properties.one: R Statement is fixed to a four-manifold with three-dimensional rest space. Proof 2.1 uses trace three and 3.1 uses a finite nine-square shear norm; a one-dimensional rest-space variant is not quantified.

lem-tgr-eckart-entropy-specialization.one: R This is a fixed four-dimensional tensor identity, not a sample or cell aggregate. Proof 2.1 adds the three heat/shear/bulk production terms and allows any individual coefficient to vanish without requiring a count-one branch.

ex-tgr-static-cosine-heat-relaxation.one: C The profile is one explicit nonconstant cosine mode plus its mean. Verification 1.1 differentiates that mode and 2.1 computes its norm as |δ|√(|Ω|/2)e^-rt; no many-mode inference is needed for this singleton-mode example.

lem-tgr-coordinate-boxes-are-compact-jor.empty: C Statement fixes m≥1 and a_j<b_j; the midpoint in every interval is an explicit point of every endpoint variant. Proof 2.1 also explicitly assigns value one to the empty product when m=1, so its thin-face cover remains valid.

def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab.empty: C Definition takes t0<t1 and three strictly ordered spatial pairs; their midpoints give a point of Ω and K. Every side-face rectangle retains the time factor and two spatial factors, so its finite Jordan integral is over a nonempty product.

def-tgr-framework-units.empty: C Definition distinguishes a family of rest slices from the supplied observer congruence and explicitly says such an orthogonal family need not exist. All unit assignments are conditional on their stated local fields; an empty collection of global rest slices supplies no missing premise or integration assertion.

lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality.empty: C Statement fixes a positive system dimension, and Proof 2.2 includes the k=0 Fourier coefficient in Z³ rather than using an empty spectrum. Zero initial data give zero through the matrix exponential in 1.2; empty finite Fourier partial sums also satisfy the coefficient bounds.

lem-tgr-cattaneo-stability-causality.empty: C Statement has four field components and positive C,κ,τ,T0,L. The lattice sum defining K includes k=0 with value one; Proof 3.1 passes finite-box inequalities to the full series, and an empty finite box contributes zero on both sides.

thm-tgr-finite-entropy-exchange-equilibr.empty: C Statement assumes r≥1 and supplies a feasible x* in the product domain, so every factor is nonempty. Proof 1.1 obtains rank two even for r=1 from one positive energy coefficient and one number coefficient; an empty cell family is explicitly excluded.

pthm-tgr-finite-stationary-response.empty: C Statement selects one prepared cell; Proof 1.1 receives its nonzero finite dimension and normalized σ from F1. For zero observables or zero control, F2 in 2.1 gives a zero kernel or zero perturbation rather than an empty-state normalization.
